transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-01-21
Start: 14:30 PST
Duration: ~46 min
Attendees: Arielle (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Nina (Redwood SA), Daniel (Copperfield CTO), Priya (Head MLOps), Samir (Infra)

Summary:
Short discovery focused on Copperfield's move from hosted endpoints to dedicated/reserved capacity. Main threads: isolation requirements for sensitive PII-ish model inputs, burst patterns around scheduled product launches, cost/latency tradeoffs and fallback policies when reserved capacity is saturated. Agreed next steps: pricing, benchmark scripts, security follow-up and on-prem feasibility.

[00:00] Arielle (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we scheduled 45 minutes so we'll go through current stack then Marcus will go into topology options and then nail down next steps. how's that sound?
[00:08] Daniel (Copperfield): yep that's great, appreciate y'all fitting us in. we've got about 20 minutes of context then want to dig into the burst questions.
[00:15] Priya (Copperfield): quick note: security will be big for us, SOC2 plus some HIPAA adjacent rules, we may need on-prem in a couple regions, but want to understand if Dedicated could meet the constraints first.
[00:25] Arielle: totally. quick qual: are you currently on any hosted LLM provider or self-host? what's generating now?
[00:33] Samir: we're running a mix — prototype on a public hosted API but production is a homegrown transformer service running on k8s with mixed GPU types. latency's not great at scale and ops is heavy.
[00:44] Marcus (Redwood): ok and what are your p95 / p99 goals? both for user-facing generation and internal batch tasks?
[00:49] Daniel: p95 for user gen has to be under 300 ms per request target for the interactive features. but we also have async summary jobs and higher-latency reranking where 1-2s is fine. our regen volume is bursty, especially around new feature launches or marketing spikes.
[01:05] Priya: also want to highlight model hygiene and context — we pass partially pseudonymized PII and some medical triage metadata, so data residency and encryption are requirements.
[01:15] Arielle: makes sense. that pushes the conversation toward dedicated pools or private. Dedicated can give you reserved GPUs with tenant isolation policies and VPC peering for data-in-transit, plus KMS integrations for keys. we'll walk through the tradeoffs.
[01:30] Marcus: quick topology framing: three common patterns we see — 1) hosted with burst to dedicated (mixed routing), 2) fully dedicated reserved pool with warm nodes and prewarm policies, 3) private (VPC/on-prem) for full control. each has different lat/cost implications.
[01:46] Daniel: can you expand on warm nodes vs prewarm and the warm pool concept? we've seen docs but want practical behavior under sudden spikes.
[01:55] Marcus: yeah. warm pool = a set of pre-initialized model instances (GPU memory allocated, KV cache warm) so first token latency is consistent. prewarm is ephemeral prestarting nodes just-in-time — faster than cold-start but costs scale with prewarm window. warm pools are reserved in Dedicated, you pay more for guaranteed capacity but get tighter SLOs. we also have hot-pools which are essentially over-provisioned capacity for very bursty windows.
[02:20] Samir: ok and eviction? if you oversubscribe and hit system limits what happens to requests?
[02:25] Marcus: by default requests are queued to stay under target latency SLOs, but you can set overflow policies: fallback to a cheaper model variant, degrade to cached responses, or route to hosted spare capacity if you have that enabled. eviction only happens at infra preemption if on spot or ephemeral instances — dedicated reserved nodes are stable.
[02:43] Priya: you mentioned model variants — do you mean smaller quantized models? we care a lot about output fidelity.
[02:50] Marcus: yeah variants typically mean quantized fp16/int8 or half-precision variants that shave cost and latency. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles by workload to keep quality within an acceptable delta — we tie that to quality monitors so you don't regress silently.
[03:08] Daniel: our main question is: for a predicted peak of 350 rps for interactive gen, what's the reasonable reserved capacity and guardrails? pricing aside for now.
[03:17] Marcus: quick ballpark depends on model and sequence length. for a Llama-like 13B at 512 tokens, on A100 type GPUs you might get X concurrent streams per GPU — sorry our internal shorthand, but we estimate roughly 25-40 qps per GPU depending on batching and latency target. for 350 rps you'd need ~10–14 GPUs plus safe margin and warm pool headroom. we'll send a modeled sizing sheet.
[03:46] Priya: and how does batching affect latency? we do many small requests (few hundred tokens) concurrently so can't batch too long.
[03:53] Marcus: continuous batching lowers cost but increases tail latency; we configure batch windows per route. Redwood Console exposes token-level latency and cost so you can tune batch windows per endpoint. for interactive features you'd keep micro-batches (1–10ms window) to preserve p95.
[04:12] Arielle: also to call out, Dedicated reserved pool supports shard pinning so tenant traffic doesn't co-locate with noisy workloads. that's different than just scheduling — it's topology level controls.
[04:22] Samir: good — that's key. we have strict blast radius limits. what about multi-tenant vs single-tenant nodes?
[04:28] Nina (Redwood): single-tenant nodes = full isolation, higher cost. Multi-tenant with fencing uses software-level isolation and quota enforcement; cheaper but more risk surface. we also have soft affinity (seg-fenced) where you get fault isolation w/out full dedicated hardware.
[04:45] Daniel: security questions — do you have FedRAMP or HIPAA posture? integrations with our KMS? audit logs?
[04:52] Arielle: we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO work in progress; HIPAA-sensitive workflows are handled in Private/on-prem packaging for now. for Dedicated we offer KMS integration (customer keys) and audit logs exported into your SIEM. we'll share the security pack.
[05:06] Priya: ok that helps. region/residency: we need nodes in eu-west and us-west and possibly ap-south later. is Dedicated region pinning available?
[05:16] Marcus: yes, you can reserve pools per-region. some GPU SKUs have limited availability so lead times apply.
[05:22] Daniel: on the burst side — launches are predictable spikes: e.g., 30 minutes at 5x baseline every Tuesday at 09:00. how would Redwood handle that if we reserve minimal capacity and want to burst?
[05:33] Marcus: two options: reserved + burst credits (short-term burst capacity we allocate if available) or prebooked scheduled burst windows where you commit to extra capacity during known windows. If you want guaranteed headroom during launch windows, prebooked is recommended. Burst credits are opportunistic.
[05:49] Samir: and what's the behavior during simultaneous bursts across customers? will burst credits be throttled?
[05:54] Marcus: yes we have priority tiers. Enterprise contracts can get higher priority. If physical capacity is exhausted, routing policies determine fallback — cheapest is degrade to cached or smaller model, or route to secondary region.
[06:08] Daniel: pricing-wise, is burst billed at on-demand hourly?
[06:12] Arielle: burst pricing is usually higher (on-demand rates) unless you precommit for scheduled windows. we can show modeled cost in the pricing sheet.
[06:19] Priya: re: telemetry and monitoring — can we get long-term token-level retention and per-route cost alerts?
[06:26] Nina: yes Console supports token-level breakdowns, alerts on cost thresholds and latency SLO breaches, and trace hooks for debugging. retention tiering is an add-on.
[06:36] Daniel: about private/on-prem — we want an eventual path for air-gapped deployments for some customers. is there a migration path from Dedicated to Private?
[06:45] Marcus: yes we have a private control plane option and on-prem package. many customers start in Dedicated and when they need full data residency or air-gap move to Private; we support export of model and config artifacts and tooling to replicate runtime. There is work involved for networking and KMS/HSM integration — we'll scope separately.
[07:02] Priya: can Redwood run a synthetic peak test against our staging to validate prewarm strategy? ideally with our exact prompts and concurrency patterns.
[07:09] Marcus: yes that's part of the benchmark playbook. we'll provide a loadgen script (k6 or locust) and a small harness for latency/throughput profiling. we'll also run a Redwood-hosted trace to simulate mixing types of requests.
[07:22] Samir: any limitations on model sizes for Dedicated? we sometimes run 70B models for internal analytics.
[07:28] Marcus: Dedicated supports larger models but orchestration changes — you may need multi-GPU sharding and different kernels; that increases complexity. We typically recommend starting with 7B/13B/34B variants for user-facing features, 70B for heavy batch. We'll list supported topologies in the doc.
[07:44] Daniel: fallback playbooks — what do you recommend as a prioritized fallback chain?
[07:49] Nina: common chain: 1) serve from prefix/KV cache (if applicable), 2) degrade to quantized/smaller variant, 3) route to Dedicated spare capacity in another region, 4) if enabled, fall back to hosted spare with lower SLA. We'll also recommend circuit-breaker thresholds and ramp-down policies.
[08:04] Priya: about SSO/SAML and RBAC controls for Console access — we need granular role separation for product vs infra team.
[08:12] Arielle: we support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and role-based policies. You can scope keys per-route and per-team. We'll include the security doc.
[08:22] Daniel: curious about your kernel/quantization strategy — do you do kernel selection automatically for nvcc/cuDNN differences?
[08:29] Marcus: yes runtime does kernel selection and will choose optimized kernels based on hardware and sequence lengths. For quantized paths we have tuned kernels; the runtime will prefer the fastest safe kernel. Sometimes the transcriptions get weird in the logs — we call that the kernel picker, ha.
[08:43] Samir: cross-region failover — how long to warm in a different region?
[08:48] Marcus: depends on whether you keep a warm pool in the failover region. If not, cold-starts can be multiple minutes. With prewarm windows you can guarantee sub-300ms startup for prewarmed nodes.
[08:58] Priya: in terms of SLAs, do you offer latency SLAs or just availability?
[09:02] Nina: Dedicated has availability SLAs and latency targets in enterprise contracts with measured SLOs per-route. The exact latency SLA varies by topology and committed warm pool.
[09:12] Daniel: ok let's talk commitment sizing — we want minimal committed GPUs to reduce cost but need confidence for launches. can Redwood run a 'what-if' for 6-month commit with scheduled weekly spikes?
[09:23] Arielle: absolutely, we'll model 6 vs 12 month commitments with burst window add-ons and show expected unit cost improvements.
[09:30] Priya: can you include suggested A/B rollout plan: start with small reserved pool for core endpoints and fall back to hosted for low-priority traffic?
[09:37] Marcus: yep that's a common rollout: 1) onboard core routes to Dedicated, 2) enable routing policies with hosted fallbacks, 3) expand reserved pool after two weeks of telemetry. We'll include a recommended rollout timeline.
[09:50] Daniel: small nit — what happens to KV cache on failover? we'll lose warm caches if routed to other region?
[09:56] Marcus: yes KV/prefix cache is regional to runtime; cross-region failover will not have the warmed cache — you can mitigate with external shared cache but that adds cross-region latency. We'll note tradeoffs.
[10:10] Arielle: okay we're at about 10 minutes left — can we summarize next steps?
[10:15] Daniel: please include the cost model with clear numbers for 350 rps profile, model mix (7B/13B), and scheduled bursts. Also include security docs and an on-prem pathway scoping.
[10:25] Arielle: action items note: we'll send pricing, benchmark harness, and security pack. Marcus will stay on the benchmark run. Nina will prep topology options. Priya and Samir will share telemetry.
[10:42] Priya: last Q — do you support HSM-backed KMS?
[10:45] Nina: yes we can integrate with customer HSM or cloud KMS; for Private we can support HSM appliances.
[10:50] Daniel: great, thanks everyone. look forward to the docs and we'll aim to have telemetry in 48 hours.
[10:55] Arielle: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invite for the security + on-prem scoping on 2025-01-28 and attach the materials. bye.

End of transcript.
